full_original_page:
# 894. Dimension-free bounded approximation for Euclidean Lipschitz-free spaces

**Area:** Functional analysis and metric geometry
**Status:** 🟡 PARTIAL
**Last checked:** 2026-10-30

## Problem statement

For a pointed subset $`M\subseteq(\mathbb R^n,\|\cdot\|_2)`$ containing $`0`$, let $`\mathrm{Lip}_0(M)`$ be the real-valued Lipschitz functions vanishing at $`0`$, with the Lipschitz norm, and define
```math
\mathcal F(M)=\overline{\mathrm{span}}\{\delta_x:x\in M\}
\subseteq\mathrm{Lip}_0(M)^*,\qquad \delta_x(f)=f(x).
```


**Question.** Is there a universal finite constant $`\Lambda\ge1`$, independent of both $`n`$ and $`M`$, such that every such $`\mathcal F(M)`$ has the $`\Lambda`$-bounded approximation property?

Here this property means that, for every norm-compact $`K\subseteq\mathcal F(M)`$ and $`\varepsilon>0`$, there exists a finite-rank bounded linear operator $`T:\mathcal F(M)\to\mathcal F(M)`$ with
```math
\|T\|\le\Lambda,\qquad \sup_{u\in K}\|Tu-u\|<\varepsilon.
```

The question asks for one finite bound, and does not require the metric approximation property $`\Lambda=1`$.

## Application

A universal approximation bound would control finite-rank approximation of transportation-cost spaces generated by Euclidean data without a dimension-dependent operator-norm loss.

## Known results and scope

The eligible source records a $`C\sqrt n`$ bound for all Euclidean subsets, following Lancien and Pernecká. The eligible paper itself also proves a dimension-independent bound for ambient nets with a fixed separation/covering ratio: an (a,b)-net is a-separated and b-dense in the whole ambient Banach space, and Theorems 2.6 and 1.5 give a K-Schauder basis with K depending only on b/a. Arbitrary Euclidean subsets need not be ambient nets, and the question seeks a constant independent of M as well as n. Pernecká and Smith prove the metric approximation property for compact subsets with suitable almost retractions from neighborhoods, including compact convex subsets. Talimdjioski's 2024 thesis explicitly retains the dimension-independent question. Later work on snowflaked metrics and property (V*) has different conclusions or dimension-dependent constants.

## References


- [Eligible source, v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.03095v1), Introduction, p. 1; [latest v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.03095v2).
- G. Lancien and E. Pernecká, *Approximation properties and Schauder decompositions in Lipschitz-free spaces*, J. Funct. Anal. 264 (2013), 2323-2334, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jfa.2013.02.012).
- E. Pernecká and R. J. Smith, *The metric approximation property and Lipschitz-free spaces over subsets of $`\mathbb R^N`$*, J. Approx. Theory 199 (2015), 29-44, [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.07036), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jat.2015.06.003), Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2.
- F. Talimdjioski, *Lipschitz-free spaces and approximation properties*, University College Dublin, 2024, p. 5, [repository](https://researchrepository.ucd.ie/bitstreams/34c6b660-d86a-47cc-894b-82530cc0cce4/download).
- M. Jung, C. Petitjean, A. Procházka and A. Quilis, *Affine Approximation in Finite Nagata Dimension and Applications to Lipschitz-free spaces*, [arXiv:2606.11723v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11723v1), Theorems A-B.

- J. Bíma, *Lipschitz-free spaces and subsets of finite-dimensional spaces*, Proc. Roy. Soc. Edinburgh A 155 (2025), 657-686, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1017/prm.2023.109), Theorem 1 (snowflaked metrics, 0<alpha<1).
- [A negative answer to Kalton's Lipschitz-free approximation question](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/preprints/Failure-of-Bounded-Approximation-in-a-Lipschitz-Free-Space-over-a-Uniformly-Discrete-Metric-Space-September-26-2026/main.pdf). The selected claimed scope was compared; no full proof certification.
- [Metric Markov cotype two for $`\ell_1`$](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/preprints/Metric-Markov-Cotype-Two-of-l1-October-5-2026/l1-markov-cotype.pdf). The selected claimed scope was compared; no full proof certification.

## Status review


**Known cases:** Each doubling-space BAP theorem has constants that can depend on dimension. The OpenAI uniformly discrete counterexample is not a finite-dimensional Euclidean subset. Snowflaked metrics, chosen affine atlases and Lipschitz extension into ell1 do not yield one dimension-independent finite-rank approximation bound inside every Euclidean-subset free space.

**Remaining target:** Resolve the full Problem statement with its stated quantifiers and hypotheses; the restricted advances discussed here do not settle that target.

sources.inspection: The counterexample is NONPROPER and uniformly discrete, with an infinite separated subset in a bounded ball. A uniformly discrete subset of finite-dimensional Euclidean space is proper, by bounded-ball total boundedness. Thus the constructed metric space cannot be a target subset with its Euclidean metric.

Universal extension of Lipschitz maps INTO l1 does not state existence of uniformly bounded finite-rank operators on F(M), or a projection onto F(M). The target spaces are arbitrary Euclidean-subset free spaces, not l1 alone.
